lines.text: Around the world, quiet networks keep everyday life running. Power. Hospitals. Banks. Most nights, nobody notices them.
Tonight, at a company called Open Forge, one machine raised an alarm. Its name is Server 4.
Server 4 was cut off from the network after a security scare. But an alarm says it kept sending data anyway.
Security wants it shut down now. That would stop any threat — and also erase its short-term memory, along with clues about what really happened. There is no undo.
Some people have started calling nights like this the Signal War: false alarms and real attacks that are hard to tell apart. Nobody knows yet whether tonight is part of it.
BOY, the Searcher, finds leads fast. He doesn't always check them.
TOOTH, the Fact-Checker, checks every source. That takes time.
LUKE, the Worst-Case Thinker, spots danger early. Sometimes he assumes the worst.
DON SOL, the Team Lead, connects the clues — but only the clues the others bring him.
Your job: tap a clue to open it. Ask your helpers what they think, and ask again when you find something new.
Choose how much you trust each helper. There is no live countdown, so take your time. Then make the call.
An attack? A mistake? Or a trap? You decide.
